name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+18 partisan lean in a safely Democratic Chicago district
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson holds a large fundraising edge over Christian Maxwell
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on district fundamentals
model.rationale: An 18-point Democratic district with an incumbent who has out-raised his challenger roughly six to one leaves Maxwell without a visible path, and markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Jackson hold.
model.watch: Fresh polling or a late wave of outside spending for Maxwell could tighten the margin, though an upset would require an extraordinary shift in this district.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 1st District, anchored on Chicago's South Side, leans Democratic by 18 points, and incumbent Jonathan Jackson is seeking another term. Jackson has raised about $515,000, far outpacing Republican Christian Maxwell's $88,000, though he ends with limited cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover the general election, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals. Prediction markets put Jackson's chances near 96 percent.

The combination of a deep Democratic lean, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge makes Maxwell's path narrow. A strong national Republican environment could trim the margin, but flipping an 18-point district would require an unusual shift. The forecast expects Jackson to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of the victory rather than the outcome.
